qt: to the Commission Mélanie Disdier (PfE), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Christophe Bay (PfE), Nicolas Bay (ECR), Christophe Gomart (PPE), Christine Singer (Renew), Fabrice Leggeri (PfE), António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Valérie Deloge (PfE), France Jamet (PfE), Silvia Sardone (PfE), Kosma Złotowski (ECR), Julie Rechagneux (PfE), Catherine Griset (PfE), Gilles Pennelle (PfE) Subject:

Fast fashion platforms (Shein, Temu, etc.) threaten the European textile industry, which has already been weakened by a wave of closures and bankruptcies. In 2024, 1 422 clothes stores and 288 manufacturers went into bankruptcy in France, including 955 compulsory liquidations1. This situation has led to job losses and trade desertification. While the Commission has examined fast fashion from the point of view of the environment, human rights and unfair commercial practices, it remains silent on the dramatic social consequences of this destruction of the European textile industry2. Ultra-fast fashion players benefit from a clear distortion of competition, including the exemption from customs duties on parcels worth less than EUR 150. 1.

Does the Commission intend to reform the Union Customs Code and promptly abolish the customs exemption for low-value consignments, which benefits Chinese ecommerce companies at the expense of EU companies?
Will it swiftly present a concrete action plan to protect EU jobs in the textile sector from unfair competition from these non-EU companies?
